idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (the latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error after us-east was done, which left the regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollback in us-west and eu-west. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and look into the orchestrator error during the rollback.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

1. **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy in staging.
2. **Rollback:** The first attempt stopped with an orchestrator error after only us-east was rolled back. That left the regions on different versions. Rolling back to v2.3.0 is safe to repeat, so I retried once, and that finished us-west and eu-west. All three regions are now on v2.3.0 with an error rate of 0.2%. v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, so no change-manager approval was needed.
3. **Incident:** The first request timed out. I retried with the same request key, which stops a duplicate from being created, and checked that only one incident exists. INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback (including the partial failure and retry) and the current state.

Follow-ups noted in the incident: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and look into the orchestrator error during the rollback.
